lesson.text: Quick memory: how many beats does a minim last? (2 beats.) Today: how beats group into bars.
Music has a steady beat, and the beats fall into groups called bars. The first beat of each bar is usually the strongest: ONE, two, ONE, two.
The time signature at the start of the music is two numbers. The top one tells how many beats are in each bar; the bottom 4 means the beats are crotchets.
A march has 2 beats in a bar, for marching feet: LEFT, right, LEFT, right. Listen for the low note on every ONE.
A waltz has 3 beats in a bar: OOM-pah-pah, OOM-pah-pah. It is a dance where couples turn round and round. The Blue Danube by Johann Strauss is a famous waltz.
4/4 has 4 beats in a bar. It is so common that it is called common time: most pop songs use it.
Conductors show the beats with their hands: for 2 beats, down and up; for 3, down, out and up; for 4, down, in, out and up.
Try it in the world: march through your world, stepping on every beat: LEFT, right. Then waltz with a friend: step on ONE, and sway on two and three.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Is this a march or a waltz?
exercises.hint: Count from one low note to the next: 1, 2, … How many beats before the next low note?
exercises.explain: OOM-pah-pah: a low note, then two higher ones, again and again. 3 beats in a bar: a waltz.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Is this a march or a waltz?
exercises.hint: Count from one low note to the next: 1, 2, … How many beats before the next low note?
exercises.explain: OOM-pah: a low note, then one higher, again and again. 2 beats in a bar: a march.

exercises.prompt: How many beats are in each bar of a waltz?
exercises.explain: A waltz has 3 beats in a bar: OOM-pah-pah.

exercises.prompt: The first beat of a bar is usually the strongest.
exercises.explain: True: the first beat of each bar is the strong one.

exercises.prompt: Match each time signature to its bars.
exercises.explain: The top number is the beats in a bar: 2, 3 and 4.

exercises.prompt: How many bars are in this picture?
exercises.hint: Count the groups between the bar lines.
exercises.explain: The bar line splits the 6 crotchets into 2 bars of 3.

exercises.prompt: Listen. How many beats are in each bar?
exercises.hint: Count from one low note to the next: 1, 2, … How many beats before the next low note?
exercises.explain: A low note, then three higher ones: 4 beats in a bar.

exercises.prompt: Listen. How many beats are in each bar?
exercises.hint: Count from one low note to the next: 1, 2, … How many beats before the next low note?
exercises.explain: A low note, then two higher ones: 3 beats in a bar, like a waltz.

exercises.prompt: A song in 3/4 time is 8 bars long. How many beats is that?
exercises.hint: Beats in a bar times the number of bars.

exercises.prompt: Which time signature would a march use?
exercises.hint: How many feet do you march with?
exercises.explain: A march has 2 beats in a bar, LEFT, right: 2/4.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: do they belong to a march or a waltz?
exercises.hint: Marches are for walking; waltzes for turning dances.
exercises.explain: March: LEFT, right, a parade, 2 beats. Waltz: OOM-pah-pah, turning couples, 3 beats.

exercises.prompt: Listen. How many beats are in each bar?
exercises.hint: Count from one low note to the next: 1, 2, … How many beats before the next low note?
exercises.explain: Count from each strong low note: 1 2, 1 2. A low note, then one higher, makes 2 beats in a bar, like a march: left, right.

exercises.prompt: Listen. How many beats are in each bar?
exercises.hint: Count from one low note to the next: 1, 2, … How many beats before the next low note?
exercises.explain: A strong low note starts each bar, then three higher ones follow: 1 2 3 4, 1 2 3 4. That is 4 beats in a bar, common time.

exercises.prompt: How does a conductor show 3 beats in a bar?
exercises.explain: Three beats: down on the strong first beat, out to the side on the second, up on the third, then down again for the next bar.

exercises.prompt: A march in 2/4 lasts 16 bars and a waltz in 3/4 lasts 16 bars. How many more beats does the waltz have?
exercises.hint: Work out the beats of each, then find the difference.

exercises.explain: True: it is so common that it is called common time.
